title: autotune: default batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for common workloads by shipping safe defaults and visibility for batching/caching and quantization. This PR combines three coordinated changes: 1) opinionated defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching in the serving runtime and gateway; 2) explicit quantization profiles for commonly used model families (Llama2, Mistral, Red-Open variants) so autotune can select compatible, high-quality quantization levels; 3) unit-economics (UEcon) tooling to surface estimated dollars-per-1000-tokens and cost delta per change and to integrate recommendations into the Autotune UI/CLI.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add runtime defaults for request-level batching and sensible per-route caching. Defaults are conservative (latency-first for small requests, throughput-first for high QPS routes) and can be overridden via route/config. Implementation touches the router, runtime executor, and default policies in the control-plane.
- Introduce quantization profile YAMLs and model metadata entries for Llama2-7B/13B, Mistral-7B, and known Redwood-verified checkpoints. Each profile includes quant-level candidate list, expected token-quality delta heuristics, and hardware compatibility tags.
- Extend the Autotune service to evaluate (simulated) unit-econ for candidate configs. Adds a lightweight cost-simulation engine and an API endpoint used by the Console to show estimated cost/savings and a recommended config with confidence scores.
- UX/CLI: small Console API surface changes and CLI command `redwood autotune recommend --route <route>` that returns the recommended profile and estimated monthly savings.
- Tests & safety: end-to-end integration tests that run in the perf-canary infra with synthetic workloads to validate latency SLAs and cost improvements, plus regression checks to ensure no >5% median-latency regressions for routes marked latency-sensitive.

Backward compatibility and risk: all changes are opt-out by route; existing routes keep previous behavior unless Autotune is enabled or defaults applied during a route create/update flow. Quant profiles are additive metadata only and do not change existing model artifacts. We added runtime feature flags to roll back batching/caching defaults quickly if needed.

Notes for reviewers: focus review on the policy selector changes in router/policy_manager and the autotune cost simulator assumptions (cost per GPU-second and cache hit estimators). See unit tests under `autotune/tests` for test cases used in evaluation. Related: ENG-3124, ENG-3180, SUP-1082.

review_comments: Daniel Ortega (2026-02-12): Overall LGTM. Two asks: 1) please call out the default batching window in nanoseconds in the doc and code comments; 2) add a small synthetic test for single-token requests to catch regressions. -- Priya: added test and documented the default 8ms batching window in both code and docs.

Marta Ivanova (2026-02-15): The cost-simulator makes a couple of simplifying assumptions around GPU amortization that could skew savings estimates for bursty workloads. Can we add a note and a toggle for using 'amortized' vs 'spot' cost models? -- Priya: added 'cost_model' parameter (amortized|spot) and a note in docs; default remains amortized for comparability with internal billing.

Samuel Green (2026-02-18): Small request: quantify the expected token-quality delta for 4-bit vs 8-bit for each profile or mark unknown. We should avoid recommending aggressive quant for latency-sensitive routes. -- Priya: quant-profile YAMLs now include estimated delta bands and the autotune recommendation filters latency-sensitive routes by default.
QA (2026-02-20): Found a flaky test in perf-canary run when cache hit-rate is exactly 0. Tests updated to seed cache with deterministic keys. -- Priya: patched tests and reran CI.
Marta Ivanova (2026-02-24): Approving after confirmatory CI run. Approved-by: Marta Ivanova

release_notes: Autotune: add conservative defaults for batching and prefix caching, add quantization profiles for common models, and ship UEcon tooling that surfaces estimated cost/savings in Console and CLI. Routes preserve existing behavior unless Autotune is enabled. See docs/autotune.md for migration and rollback steps.
